nodes.question: Change the black DVD to white while retaining its identity as a DVD.
nodes.criteria: Judge only the requested transformation, using both support observations. Return yes when the DVD is visibly white rather than black and retains its identity as a DVD. Return no only when there is sufficient evidence that no requested change has progressed—for example, the DVD remains black and retains its identity. Return partial when the color change has progressed but the DVD is not yet white, or when the DVD is white but its identity as a DVD has been lost. Unrelated edits do not count. If the evidence does not establish one of these outcomes, return unresolved. Support observations are evidence, not independent completion credit.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. You receive no reference label or optimization feedback. Return status, evidence, reported confidence (0..1 or null), and used_dependency_ids naming every supplied context check_id exactly once in saved order.
Supports receive source and edited images. Answer only the saved proposition using its binding and criteria. Use pass/fail/unknown. Context is advisory unless listed in required_dependencies. A negative context observation is usable evidence. Unknown, skipped, or invalid context is not a failure and must not stop an independent image inspection. Inspect the images yourself; do not repeat a parent's answer. Return unknown when the relevant fact cannot be established. Confidence reports confidence in this answer, not calibrated correctness.
Fulfillment receives NO images. Use only saved support evidence, original instruction/rubric and frozen composition criteria. Return complete/partial/absent/unknown. Supporting passes answer specific propositions, not a count of completed edits. Their polarity can differ. Apply saved alternatives: optional uncertainty need not prevent a known outcome, but a required unresolved fact makes that outcome unresolved. Never invent a visual fact or convert missing evidence into failure. A conditional skip is not non-applicability. All applicable requested outcomes complete gives yes; no requested progress gives no; known progress short of completion gives partial. Unrelated changes are not progress.

fulfillment: The node’s binding is too vague and its traces appear to accept a white disc anywhere as the target. In the images, the original DVD is the small rectangular item near the center; the edited image shows two white discs, while the original item is no longer clearly identifiable at that location. Do not infer that the DVD was recolored merely because white discs are visible or because a disc-shaped object has a center hole. Tighten target binding to track the specific original DVD across the edit, and require evidence that this same object changed from black to white and retained DVD identity. Evaluate the joint requested transformation using the support observations, distinguishing complete fulfillment from partial progress or no progress; do not treat support checks as independent completion credit. The repeated high-confidence “yes” traces suggest a systematic target-correspondence/evidence problem, not uncertainty to resolve by lowering confidence. The reference “no” is an aggregate constraint, not atomic ground truth; use it to investigate the mismatch rather than force a label. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.
s2: Tighten the binding to the specific source object using its location and appearance: the small rectangular DVD case near the image center, not any disc-shaped object in the edited image. This node checks retained DVD identity, so require evidence that the corresponding object can be tracked across the edit and is still visibly identifiable as a DVD; a center hole or another white disc alone is insufficient. If correspondence or identity is unclear, return unknown rather than confidently passing. Keep this support check distinct from the separate color-change criterion, and ensure downstream fulfillment combines both observations to distinguish partial progress from complete fulfillment or no progress. The repeated high-confidence passes indicate systematic target-binding/evidence failure, not a reason to lower confidence or force the aggregate reference label. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.
s1: Tighten the binding to the specific DVD shown in the source image: the small rectangular, printed item near the center, and require cross-image correspondence before judging its color or retained identity. In the edit, two white discs are visible, but neither is clearly the same printed rectangular source object; do not count a nearby white disc or a center hole as proof that the DVD was recolored. Keep this support node focused on whether the corresponding object remains identifiable as a DVD, distinct from the separate color-change check, and return unknown when correspondence or identity is not established. The repeated high-confidence passes indicate a systematic binding/evidence error, not a reason to lower confidence or force the aggregate reference label. Preserve downstream evaluation of complete versus partial progress; no transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated.
